as_told.title: Life magazine withholds the Zapruder film under C.D. Jackson

plain: The story goes that after President John F. Kennedy was shot in 1963, the best film of the killing was held back from the public in a way that hid part of what happened. The film is the Zapruder film, a home movie that Michels calls "the clearest footage of the assassination." A researcher named Jeremy Riss says the man who led its release was Charles Douglas Jackson, and he says it without naming a source. Michels tells the rest himself, also without a source. He says Life, a big American news magazine, bought the film. Then, he says, instead of showing it in full, "they only published black and white stills with certain key frames missing." Michels also says the film stayed held back into the 1970s, which Riss does not say. The two tell it independently, a researcher and the host, and they agree on Jackson's role. If it were true, it would mean one well-placed man shaped what the country was allowed to see of the assassination.
